method.normalisation: views / median views of the 30 mature (>=7 days old) posts closest in age; provisional posts excluded from rankings
method.tests: permutation test on medians, 5000 shuffles, no multiple-comparison correction

limitations: Only public preview data: views (rounded by Telegram, for example 2.19K), reactions (visible counts only), dates and text. No reach, no unique viewers, no demographics, no click or conversion data, and no replies or forward counts (the preview does not expose them for these channels).

Views accumulate with age and a single snapshot cannot show the curve. Posts younger than 7 days are excluded from rankings and baselines (1 chesscom_ru post, 7 EdChess posts). A second snapshot was taken a few hours after the first and stored as a separate observation, but that gap is too short to estimate growth. Re-run the scraper weekly to build real age curves.

Normalisation: each post is compared with the median views of the 30 mature posts closest to it in age, which also controls for audience growth and decline. This controls for time, not for topic or for paid promotion.
Subscribers are the current count; the past subscriber count of each channel is unknown. EdChess early posts (2025) have lower views partly because the channel was smaller.
Content-type and hook labels are rule-based first passes with manual corrections on the lists shown. They are judgement calls. Medal-list and news categories overlap.
Statistical tests are permutation tests on medians with no correction for the 24 comparisons made; read p-values below about 0.01 as suggestive and anything near 0.05 as noise.
Images and video are not visible in the preview and were deliberately not downloaded, so visual hooks, thumbnails and meme content could not be judged. Image-only posts are therefore a known gap.
Three EdChess posts show 8x to 32x baseline views; they look paid or partner-boosted. They are shown but should not be read as organic virality.
The two channels are not comparable by raw views: chesscom_ru has about 0.50 views per subscriber, EdChess about 0.06. EdChess's subscriber base is large but its posts reach a small share of it.

Reddit: three content requests (the .json endpoint twice, RSS once) were made to test access before robots.txt was read, then robots.txt itself, then one more request to the r/AnarchyChess page after it had been read, which was a mistake. reddit.com/robots.txt disallows all automated access, so no further Reddit requests were made and no Reddit post data was used or stored.
YouTube channel pages (youtube.com/@handle, about 20 requests, allowed by its robots.txt) were opened only to confirm the handles resolve; YouTube feeds were not requested.
The vidIQ index supplied YouTube channel ids and subscriber counts; those figures are third-party estimates. The YouTube Data API itself was not called.

formats_ranked.evidence: EdChess, n=50 posts: 16.0 vs 11.3 reactions per 1K views (permutation p=0.003); reach +5% vs baseline (p=0.054). 10 of its top 25 reaction-rate posts use it.
formats_ranked.adaptation: Tactics, slot 1. One position image, four candidate moves each mapped to a reaction, reveal the same day as a threaded reply. Our own positions (Lichess CC0 data or verified games), our own explanation.
formats_ranked.guardrail: Do not turn the reactions into a prediction market or a prize draw. No "react to earn". EdChess adds a tournament line mentioning $TON earnings under most vote posts; its reactions themselves are not rewarded, but the funnel claim is exactly what we must not copy.

formats_ranked.format: Short culture caption or image-only meme
formats_ranked.evidence: chesscom_ru: short captions n=10 at 39.4 vs 18.6 reactions per 1K (p<0.001); image-only posts n=20 at 29.1 vs 18.2 (p<0.001); reach flat (1.02 vs 1.02). 15 of the top 25 reaction-rate posts are this family (captions, emoji-only, image-only, birthdays, greetings).
formats_ranked.strength: Strong for engagement, none for reach
formats_ranked.adaptation: Chess Culture, slot 4. One restrained joke about a real chess feeling, on our own licensed art (violet rook, outlined CHESS wordmark). Never reuse a community meme image.
formats_ranked.guardrail: Competitor images are not visible in the preview, so the visual hook is unmeasured. Humour must not mock real players or young players.

formats_ranked.format: Record or first-ever claim with a number up front
formats_ranked.evidence: chesscom_ru: record/superlative n=7 at 1.27x baseline vs 1.02 (p=0.008), 30.2 vs 18.9 reactions per 1K (p=0.034); number-first opening n=13 at 1.08x (p=0.35). The top two posts by normalised views use a number-first or rating-ladder hook.
formats_ranked.strength: Moderate (small n for records; effect matches the top lists)
formats_ranked.adaptation: Chess News, slot 2. A verified record, then one original lesson from the position that produced it. The number leads the first line.
formats_ranked.guardrail: Verify against a primary source before posting; never state a record you cannot cite.

formats_ranked.format: "This day in chess" history, birthdays and tributes
formats_ranked.evidence: chesscom_ru: history/anniversary/tribute n=8 at 37.4 vs 18.7 reactions per 1K (p=0.002); the two highest reaction-rate posts of the channel are birthdays (62.9 and 54.0 per 1K).
formats_ranked.strength: Moderate (n=8; consistent in the top list)
formats_ranked.adaptation: Chess Culture or News, slot 4 about twice a week. A dated fact plus the decisive position from that game. Our own copy.
formats_ranked.guardrail: Tributes after a death are not engagement material: use a plain, factual tone and no promotion beside them.

formats_ranked.format: Puzzle prompt with a same-day reveal
formats_ranked.evidence: chesscom_ru: puzzle prompts n=20 at 1.08x baseline (p=0.23) with 15.2 reactions per 1K (below the channel median of 19, p=0.13): steady reach, weak engagement because answers happen elsewhere.
formats_ranked.adaptation: Tactics, slot 1, always combined with format 1 so the answer happens in the post. Reveal as a threaded reply the same day.
formats_ranked.guardrail: Open-loop rule from STRATEGY.md: the payoff must land in the same asset sequence.

formats_ranked.evidence: chesscom_ru: quote/interview n=10 at 1.16x baseline and 30.9 reactions per 1K; the fourth-ranked post by reach is a quote plus a question (1.99x, 9.4K views).
formats_ranked.adaptation: Chess News, slot 2. A short public quote (under about 15 words), exact and attributed, then our chess explanation of the position it refers to.
formats_ranked.guardrail: Quote accurately and briefly; no invented quotes; link the primary source.

formats_ranked.evidence: chesscom_ru: audience prompts n=11 at 0.98x baseline, 20.5 reactions per 1K (neutral); the "caption this photo" post is in the top 25 by reactions, the chat-screenshot post ranks 8th by reach, but the revived "brilliant move from a subscriber" series sits in the bottom decile (0.84x).

compliance: Any post that mentions a stake, a payout, a pot, USDT matches or settlement must carry "18+ only" and "you can lose your stake" in the same post, in the same language, above the link. Do not shorten to an icon.

No income, "earn", "win money", salary, passive-income or profit-expectation language. This is the main contrast with EdChess, whose headlines promise $TON, $GRAM and USDT prizes while only 5 of its 329 posts show any risk wording.

Never pair wager content with youth content: no wager post within six hours of a post about players under 18, school chess, kids, juniors or youth events, and never on the same slot sequence as Academy material aimed at beginners or children. Chess news channels regularly cover child prodigies (for example a 12-year-old grandmaster-norm story in chesscom_ru), so the news slot needs a youth check before the evening slot.
No fake urgency, countdowns, limited seats or "last chance" copy unless a real, sourced deadline exists. Competitors use "only N days left" for in-app quests; do not copy that.
Restrict wager messaging by jurisdiction exactly as the product does; confirm the current geo rules with the product owner before the first Match Rules post (not verified here).
Telegram's own advertising and bot rules may restrict crypto and gambling content in paid placements; check the current policy before buying any promotion (not verified here).

Reuse: competitor text, photos (FIDE and photographer credits), clips and memes stay theirs. We keep only short evidence excerpts in internal research. Rebuild the idea with our own position, wording and licensed brand art.
Anything quoted from a person must be exact, short and attributed; obituaries and tributes get no commercial context.
Public view counts are not reach and not conversion. Do not publish claims about our audience or results until attribution (STRATEGY.md measurement plan) exists.
